short: A protracted defense of the Danish capital that broke the Swedish attempt to erase Denmark.
full:
Unsatisfied with the massive gains of the Treaty of Roskilde, Charles X Gustav of Sweden renewed hostilities in August 1658 with the explicit goal of entirely subjugating Denmark as a sovereign state. Swedish forces rapidly advanced and laid siege to Copenhagen, the last significant Danish stronghold. King Frederick III refused to flee, rallying the city's inhabitants—including students and burghers—to construct defenses and repel the invaders.

The siege's turning point occurred on 11 February 1659, when a major Swedish assault across the ice was bloodily repulsed with heavy casualties. Supported by a Dutch relief fleet that broke the Swedish naval blockade, Copenhagen held out for over a year and a half. The city's survival prevented the total annexation of Denmark and forced a military stalemate, ultimately leading to peace negotiations following Charles X Gustav's death.
